title: Working with vectors
description:
Write these functions:

```rust
fn running_totals(values: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>             // [1, 2, 3] gives [1, 3, 6]
fn remove_negatives(values: &mut Vec<i32>)                 // in place, keeping the order
fn merge_sorted(a: &[i32], b: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>          // two sorted slices into one sorted vector, in one pass
fn top_n(values: &[i32], n: usize) -> Vec<i32>             // the n largest, largest first (fewer if there are fewer)
fn unique_in_order(values: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>             // without repeats, first occurrences kept, in order
```
hints: `values.retain(|&v| v >= 0)` keeps the items that pass the test and removes the rest, in place.

For `top_n`, copy the values (`values.to_vec()`), `sort()` them, then `pop()` the largest ones off the end until you have `n`. For `unique_in_order`, `out.contains(&v)` tells whether a value is already in the result.
